title: 2026 budget adopted with 3.68% township tax increase
subtitle: Staffing strategy, Bissell Park pad design, downtown service levels, affordable housing work and business park pricing also covered.
overview: Council deemed the 2026 budget adopted {{vote:m8}} after a full day of review. Staff reported the township's share of the tax bill at 3.86% in the budget book. Late insurance savings of about $43,000 lowered that to 3.68%, and council chose by informal consensus to take that reduction in the levy rather than add it to asset management. The proposed staffing strategy stayed intact after the parking-lot review, including the policy and housing planner and the three labourer positions.

Council also passed the 2026 fees and charges by-law {{vote:m4}}, which raises most fees by about 2.5%, and approved the 2026 Draft Business Plan {{vote:m6}}. Staff will return in the first quarter of 2026 with two or three affordable housing ideas for a county funding application {{vote:m5}}.

Other decisions set 2026 downtown service levels {{vote:m1}}, sent the Bissell Park multi-use pad to detailed design {{vote:m2}}, and kept the business park price at $450,000 per acre {{vote:m3}}. Residents will see more downtown garbage collection where needed, paid parking, and year-round trail maintenance in 2026.

decisions.detail: Council waived the remaining amendment and veto periods and deemed the 2026 budget adopted {{vote:m8}}.
Council approved the business plan that links the 2026 budget to the strategic plan {{vote:m6}}.
Staff will bring back two or three high-level affordable housing initiatives in the first quarter of 2026 for a Wellington County Community Housing Development Fund application {{vote:m5}}.
Council endorsed the 2026 levels of service in the downtown BIA catchments, to start in January 2026 within the draft operating budget {{vote:m1}}.
Staff were directed to proceed to detailed design and bring back refined costs for the pad options {{vote:m2}}.
The 2025 pricing policy continues for 2026 with a base price of $450,000 per acre {{vote:m3}}.

debate: On downtown service levels, councillors raised overflowing garbage receptacles in Fergus and the lack of weekend pickup. Staff said garbage collection is a flexible cost and can be increased if needed. Others asked for more benches, bike racks and wayfinding.

Some councillors questioned why the township supports Monster Month installation in Elora and asked whether equivalent support should extend to other events or to Fergus. Staff said a future special events policy would sort out who pays for what.

On Bissell Park, some councillors questioned the cost of the pad and the plan to put refrigeration lines in now, preferring a like-for-like replacement and setting aside part of the budget for other parks needs. Others said lines cannot be added later and the option should stay open. Staff noted the recommendation keeps both options until detailed design.

On staffing, one councillor asked whether the purchasing and risk position could be part-time to trim the tax rate, and another suggested a part-time or mid-year start for the housing planner. Staff said purchasing is already a bottleneck and the planner also covers overdue policy work.

On the insurance savings, some councillors favoured putting them toward asset management, which is under its 2% target. Most preferred lowering the levy because of affordability pressures. The saving works out to about $3 a year on an average home.
